question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

She is an M.Sc. graduate (a)/ and works as a unit manager (b)/ at an NGO in Pune. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound and not on the spelling. "M.Sc." is pronounced "em-ess-see" (vowel sound), so "an M.Sc."; "unit" begins with the consonant sound /yoo/, so "a unit"; "NGO" is pronounced "en-jee-oh" (vowel sound), so "an NGO".

◦ Sentence as given: She is an M.Sc. graduate and works as a unit manager at an NGO in Pune.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "an M.Sc. graduate" is proper, because the first letter is pronounced "em", which is a vowel sound.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "a unit manager" is proper, because "unit" begins with the consonant sound /yoo/.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "an NGO in Pune." is proper, because the first letter is pronounced "en", which is a vowel sound.

 

NOTE

 

• letters pronounced with a vowel sound (A, E, F, H, I, L, M, N, O, R, S, X): an M.Sc., an NGO, an MP, an FIR, an SI; other letters: a B.Sc., a PhD, a CEO, a UN official.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Governments should provide (a)/ free medical treatment (b)/ to poor (c)/ and the elderly. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The" + an adjective names a whole group of people (the poor, the rich, the elderly, the injured). "Poor" alone is only an adjective, so "to poor" must be "to the poor".

◦ Corrected sentence: Governments should provide free medical treatment to the poor and the elderly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Governments should provide" is proper, with a plural noun taking no article for a general statement and a modal followed by the base form.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "free medical treatment" is proper, because "treatment" is used as an uncountable noun.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and the elderly." is proper, with "the" used before the adjective "elderly" to name a group.

 

NOTE

 

• the + adjective = a plural group: the poor, the blind, the young, the injured; it takes a plural verb: The poor need help.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Mobile phones (a)/ became affordable (b)/ for the middle class (c)/ only in 1990s. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Decades and centuries take the definite article: "the 1990s", "the twentieth century". So "in 1990s" must be "in the 1990s". Single years take no article ("in 1995").

◦ Corrected sentence: Mobile phones became affordable for the middle class only in the 1990s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Mobile phones" is a proper plural subject, with no article needed for a general statement.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "became affordable" is proper, because "became" is a linking verb followed by an adjective.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "for the middle class" is proper, with "the" used before the name of a social class.

 

NOTE

 

• in the 1990s, in the twentieth century, in the 1980s; but a single year takes no article: in 1995.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The delegates (a)/ travelled by the train (b)/ from Delhi (c)/ to Jaipur. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With "by" + a means of transport, no article is used: by train, by bus, by road, by air. So "by the train" must be "by train".

◦ Corrected sentence: The delegates travelled by train from Delhi to Jaipur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The delegates" is a proper plural subject, with "the" used for a specific group.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "from Delhi" is proper, because the name of a city takes no article.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to Jaipur." is proper, because the name of a city takes no article.

 

NOTE

 

• by train, by bus, by air, on foot (no article); but for a particular vehicle: He left his bag on the bus.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The coach patted him on back (a)/ after he scored (b)/ his maiden century (c)/ for the state team. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a person is the object and a part of his body follows a preposition (pat him on the back, hit him on the head, catch him by the arm), the article "the" is used and not a possessive. So "on back" must be "on the back".

◦ Corrected sentence: The coach patted him on the back after he scored his maiden century for the state team.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "after he scored" is a proper past clause of time.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "his maiden century" is proper, with the possessive "his" used and no article needed.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "for the state team." is proper, with "the" used for a specific team.

 

NOTE

 

• patted him on the back, hit him on the head, caught her by the hand, looked him in the eye; but with the subject's own body part: He shook his head.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

At the function, (a)/ the Chief Minister Sharma (b)/ inaugurated the new (c)/ terminal building. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a title stands directly before a name, no article is used: "Chief Minister Sharma". "The" is used when the title stands alone or in apposition ("the Chief Minister", "Mr. Sharma, the Chief Minister"). So "the Chief Minister Sharma" must be "Chief Minister Sharma".

◦ Corrected sentence: At the function, Chief Minister Sharma inaugurated the new terminal building.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "At the function," is a proper introductory phrase, with "the function" as a specific event.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "inaugurated the new" is proper, with a simple past verb followed by a specific object.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "terminal building." is proper, completing the noun phrase "the new terminal building".

 

NOTE

 

• President Murmu, Dr. Rao, Captain Kohli (no article before title + name); the President of India, Mr. Sharma, the Chief Minister (title alone).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The temple attracts (a)/ pilgrims from (b)/ across the country, (c)/ and the most of them are farmers. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Most of" (= the majority of) takes no "the" before "most". "The most" is used only as a superlative (the most beautiful). So "the most of them" must be "most of them".

◦ Corrected sentence: The temple attracts pilgrims from across the country, and most of them are farmers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The temple attracts" is a proper singular subject and verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "pilgrims from" is proper, with a plural noun taking no article for a general statement.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "across the country," is a proper prepositional phrase, with "the country" as a specific, known area.

 

NOTE

 

• most of the villagers, most of them (majority); the most beautiful (superlative) — never the most of.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The double price (a)/ is being charged by the company (b)/ for the same (c)/ service. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Words such as double, twice, half, all and both come before "the" and not after it. So "The double price" must be "Double the price".

◦ Corrected sentence: Double the price is being charged by the company for the same service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is being charged by the company" is a proper singular passive verb, agreeing with "price".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "for the same" is proper, because "same" always takes "the".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "service." is proper, as a singular countable noun that is already introduced by "the same".

 

NOTE

 

• double the price, twice the size, half the cost, all the students, both the brothers (predeterminer + "the" + noun); the same, the only always take "the".

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The interview was (a)/ scheduled for (b)/ an half hour, (c)/ but it lasted longer. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Half" comes before the article: "half an hour", "half a kilometre". The pattern "an half hour" is wrong, so it must be "half an hour".

◦ Corrected sentence: The interview was scheduled for half an hour, but it lasted longer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The interview was" is a proper singular subject with "was".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "scheduled for" is proper, with "for" used before a period of time.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "but it lasted longer." is a proper clause of contrast, with the simple past "lasted".

 

NOTE

 

• half an hour, half a kilometre, an hour and a half; "a" or "an" is chosen by the sound of the word that follows it.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Ill with fever, (a)/ the boy missed (b)/ the annual exam (c)/ and stayed in the bed. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bed, school, church, college and prison take no article when they are used for their main purpose (sleeping, studying, worship). Staying ill at home is "in bed", so "in the bed" must be "in bed".

◦ Corrected sentence: Ill with fever, the boy missed the annual exam and stayed in bed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Ill with fever," is a proper adjective phrase describing the boy.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the boy missed" is a proper singular subject with a simple past verb.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the annual exam" is proper, with "the" used for a specific exam.

 

NOTE

 

• main purpose — in bed, go to school, go to church (to worship); the building itself — went to the church to take photographs, went to the school to meet the principal.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Lake Superior, (a)/ the largest of the Great Lakes, (b)/ lies between the Canada (c)/ and the United States. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The name of a single country takes no article, whereas the names of plural or union states take "the" (the United States, the Netherlands). So "the Canada" must be "Canada".

◦ Corrected sentence: Lake Superior, the largest of the Great Lakes, lies between Canada and the United States.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Lake Superior," is proper, because the name of a single lake takes no article.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the largest of the Great Lakes," is proper, with "the" used before the superlative and before the name of a group of lakes.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and the United States." is proper, because "the" is used before this union name.

 

NOTE

 

• no article — Canada, India, Japan, Lake Victoria, Mount Everest; "the" — the United States, the United Kingdom, the Philippines, the Great Lakes, the Himalayas.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Over hundred years old, (a)/ the temple still (b)/ attracts thousands of (c)/ pilgrims every year. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a number word such as hundred, thousand or dozen means an exact single unit, it takes "a" or "one". So "over hundred years old" must be "over a hundred years old".

◦ Corrected sentence: Over a hundred years old, the temple still attracts thousands of pilgrims every year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the temple still" is proper, with the adverb "still" placed before the main verb.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "attracts thousands of" is proper, because "thousands of" is an indefinite plural expression with no article.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "pilgrims every year." is proper, with a plural noun and "every" followed by a singular noun.

 

NOTE

 

• a hundred, a thousand, a dozen, a couple of; but hundreds of, thousands of (no article).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Ships from (a)/ Chennai sail across (b)/ Bay of Bengal (c)/ to Southeast Asia. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The names of seas, bays, gulfs and oceans take the definite article "the". So "Bay of Bengal" must be "the Bay of Bengal".

◦ Corrected sentence: Ships from Chennai sail across the Bay of Bengal to Southeast Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Ships from" is proper, with a plural noun taking no article for a general statement.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "Chennai sail across" is proper, because the name of a city takes no article and the plural verb "sail" agrees with "Ships".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to Southeast Asia." is proper, because the name of a region takes no article.

 

NOTE

 

• the Bay of Bengal, the Gulf of Mannar, the Arabian Sea, the Indian Ocean, the Persian Gulf; single lakes and peaks take no article: Lake Chilika, Mount Kailash.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Rohan is ill, so he will not go to the school today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. school.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A place such as school, college, hospital, prison or church takes no article when it is visited for its primary purpose (studying, treatment, imprisonment, worship). Rohan would go to school to study, so "the school" must be "school".

◦ Corrected sentence: Rohan is ill, so he will not go to school today.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "a school" — "a" treats the school as one building among many, and it is not used when the place is visited for its purpose.

 

• Option 3: "schools" — the plural does not suit "go to … today", which refers to Rohan's daily attendance for study.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because "the school" points to the building and not to the purpose of studying.

 

NOTE

 

• go to school, go to college, go to church (to pray), be in prison (as a prisoner); but with another purpose: The father went to the school to meet the principal.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

He has ___ friends in this city, so he often feels lonely.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. few.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Few" (without "a") has a negative sense (= hardly any), while "a few" has a positive sense (= some). The sentence says that he "often feels lonely", so the idea is negative, and the correct word is "few".

◦ Complete sentence: He has few friends in this city, so he often feels lonely.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "a few" — "a few" means "some" and has a positive sense, which does not fit with "feels lonely".

 

• Option 3: "the few" — "the few" points to a limited, known group (usually followed by "who / that"), and the sentence gives no such reference.

 

• Option 4: "a little" — "a little" is used with uncountable nouns, and "friends" is a plural countable noun.

 

NOTE

 

• few / a few / the few + plural countable noun; little / a little / the little + uncountable noun: Few people came (hardly any), A few people came (some), The few people who came were happy.

question: Select the sentence in which the article is used correctly.
option_1: He works for Reserve Bank of India as a clerk.
option_2: The Diwali is celebrated with great joy across India.
option_3: We visited Red Fort on Republic Day.
option_4: The Supreme Court is the highest court of appeal in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The Supreme Court is the highest court of appeal in India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 4 is correct. The names of courts, famous buildings and institutions take the definite article "the" ("the Supreme Court"), and the superlative "highest" also takes "the".

◦ Correct sentence: The Supreme Court is the highest court of appeal in India.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "He works for Reserve Bank of India as a clerk." — the name of an institution built with "of" takes "the": "the Reserve Bank of India".

 

• Option 2: "The Diwali is celebrated with great joy across India." — the names of festivals take no article: "Diwali is celebrated …".

 

• Option 3: "We visited Red Fort on Republic Day." — the names of famous monuments take "the": "the Red Fort".

 

NOTE

 

• the Red Fort, the Taj Mahal, the Reserve Bank of India, the Supreme Court; but Diwali, Eid, Republic Day (festivals take no article).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The number of students were absent from the class because of the strike.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A number of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "A number of" means "many" and takes a plural noun and a plural verb ("A number of students were absent"). "The number of" means "the total count" and takes a singular verb ("The number of students was …"). The verb here is the plural "were", so "The number of" must be "A number of".

◦ Corrected sentence: A number of students were absent from the class because of the strike.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Number of" — the singular countable noun "number" cannot stand without an article.

 

• Option 3: "The numbers of" — "the numbers of" refers to figures or statistics, and it does not give the sense of "many" that the sentence needs.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because "The number of" needs the singular verb "was", and the plural "were" does not agree with it.

 

NOTE

 

• A number of students were absent (= many students, plural verb); The number of students was small (= the total, singular verb).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

She is ___ intelligent a girl that everyone in the class admires her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. so.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word order "so / as / too / how + adjective + a / an + noun" is used with "so … that" (cause and result). So "so intelligent a girl that …" is correct. "Such" is used in a different order: "such + a + adjective + noun".

◦ Complete sentence: She is so intelligent a girl that everyone in the class admires her.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "such" — "such" comes before "a" ("such an intelligent girl"), and it cannot be followed by "adjective + a + noun".

 

• Option 2: "too" — "too" gives a negative sense and is followed by "to + verb"; it does not take a "that" clause.

 

• Option 4: "quite" — "quite" is placed before "a" ("quite an intelligent girl"), and it does not form a result clause.

 

NOTE

 

• so good a player = such a good player; as clever a boy as; too heavy a burden to carry; how big a mistake.

question: Select the sentence in which the article is used correctly.
option_1: The cow is a useful animal for farmers.
option_2: The man is a social animal.
option_3: The gold is a precious metal.
option_4: The nature has given us many gifts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The cow is a useful animal for farmers.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 1 is correct. A singular countable noun with "the" can stand for a whole class or species ("The cow" means "cows in general"). However, "man" (= mankind), material nouns and general abstract nouns take no article.

◦ Correct sentence: The cow is a useful animal for farmers.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "The man is a social animal." — "man" used for mankind as a whole takes no article: "Man is a social animal".

 

• Option 3: "The gold is a precious metal." — a material noun used in a general sense takes no article: "Gold is a precious metal".

 

• Option 4: "The nature has given us many gifts." — "nature" used as a general abstract noun takes no article: "Nature has given us many gifts".

 

NOTE

 

• The cow is a useful animal, The tiger is a wild animal (a whole species); Man is mortal, Gold is costly, Nature is kind (no article).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

A long queue of parents stood ___ the school gate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. in front of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed prepositional phrase "in front of" (= before, facing) takes no article. Phrases with "the front" carry a different meaning, such as "in the front of" (= inside the front part of something).

◦ Complete sentence: A long queue of parents stood in front of the school gate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "in the front of" — this means "in the front part of" something that has an inside (a bus or a hall), and it does not mean "facing" the gate.

 

• Option 3: "on the front of" — this means "on the front surface of" something (on the front of the shirt), and it does not suit a queue standing before a gate.

 

• Option 4: "at front of" — this is not an idiom in English, and the correct fixed phrase is "in front of".

 

NOTE

 

• in front of (= before): stood in front of the bus; in the front of (= in the front part): sat in the front of the bus.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Meena has been learning Kathak for the last five years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement required.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. "For" is used with a period of time, and "the last + number + time word" takes the definite article "the". So "for the last five years" is correct with the present perfect continuous.

◦ Sentence as given: Meena has been learning Kathak for the last five years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "for last five years" — "the" is required before "last" when it is followed by a number and a time word: "for the last five years".

 

• Option 2: "since the last five years" — "since" is used with a point in time (since 2021), and not with a period of time.

 

• Option 3: "from the last five years" — "from" does not express a period of time that continues up to now.

 

NOTE

 

• for the last five years / for the past five years (a period); since 2021 (a point in time); but last year, last week (a single time unit just before now) take no article.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

Many ___ student in this village has benefited from the scholarship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The pattern "many a + singular noun + singular verb" means "many + plural noun" ("many a student has" = "many students have"). The article is "a" before the consonant sound of "student", and the verb "has" is singular.

◦ Complete sentence: Many a student in this village has benefited from the scholarship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "the" — "many" is not followed by "the" in this pattern.

 

• Option 2: "an" — "an" is used before a vowel sound, and "student" begins with a consonant sound.

 

• Option 4: No article needed — "many student" is wrong, because "many" takes a plural noun, and a singular noun after "many" needs "a".

 

NOTE

 

• many a student has = many students have; many an actor has (before a vowel sound); a great many people.

question: Select the sentence in which the article is used correctly.
option_1: He returned home in the evening and slept at once.
option_2: She woke up at the dawn to catch the first train.
option_3: The ambulance reached the hospital in the time to save the patient.
option_4: The bus stopped for the fifteen minutes at the border.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. He returned home in the evening and slept at once.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 1 is correct. "In the morning / afternoon / evening" take "the", while "at night, at noon, at dawn and at midnight" take none. The fixed phrases "in time" and "for + a period of time" also take no article.

◦ Correct sentence: He returned home in the evening and slept at once.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "She woke up at the dawn to catch the first train." — "at dawn" is a fixed phrase and takes no article.

 

• Option 3: "The ambulance reached the hospital in the time to save the patient." — "in time" (= early enough) is a fixed phrase and takes no article.

 

• Option 4: "The bus stopped for the fifteen minutes at the border." — "for" + a period of time takes no article: "for fifteen minutes".

 

NOTE

 

• in the morning / afternoon / evening but at night / at noon / at dawn / at midnight; in time (early enough) / on time (punctual); for ten minutes.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

___ are known for their punctuality and hard work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The Japanese.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A nationality word that does not take "-s" in the plural (Japanese, Chinese, Swiss, Dutch, British) takes "the" when it names the whole people of a country. So "The Japanese" is correct.

◦ Complete sentence: The Japanese are known for their punctuality and hard work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Japanese" — this kind of nationality word needs "the" when it stands for the whole people, so it cannot be used alone as the subject.

 

• Option 3: "A Japanese" — this names one person and takes a singular verb, but the sentence has the plural verb "are".

 

• Option 4: "Japaneses" — "Japanese" has the same form in the singular and the plural, and it does not take "-s".

 

NOTE

 

• the Japanese, the Chinese, the Swiss, the Dutch, the British; but Indians, Germans, Americans (plural in "-s", no article for a general statement).

question: Select the sentence in which the article is used correctly.
option_1: Many people suffered from the dengue last monsoon.
option_2: The boy missed the match because he had bad cold.
option_3: The accident victim is in the critical condition.
option_4: Malaria is spread by the bite of a female mosquito.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Malaria is spread by the bite of a female mosquito.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 4 is correct. The names of diseases take no article ("Malaria"), while "the bite of a female mosquito" correctly uses "the" before a noun identified by an "of" phrase and "a" for a general singular noun.

◦ Correct sentence: Malaria is spread by the bite of a female mosquito.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Many people suffered from the dengue last monsoon." — the names of diseases take no article: "suffered from dengue".

 

• Option 2: "The boy missed the match because he had bad cold." — "cold" is a countable ailment and needs "a": "a bad cold".

 

• Option 3: "The accident victim is in the critical condition." — "in critical condition" is a fixed phrase and takes no article.

 

NOTE

 

• no article: malaria, dengue, typhoid, cancer; with "a": a cold, a fever, a headache, a cough; in critical condition, in good health.
